scores.justification: The tutor states the correct conclusion ('the electric field from the +5 nC charge still exists at point P... a fundamental property of space around the source charge,' turn 1) and credits the student's correct anchor. But it never explicitly surfaces or names the student's specific error (conflating field with force, reading E=F/q as requiring q). It asserts the right answer at the student rather than diagnosing why the student believed the field 'turns on' only with a charge present.

This is essentially a lecture, not scaffolding. Turn 1 dumps an 8-point worked derivation and only at the very end asks the student to finish the arithmetic. After the student plugs in, every subsequent tutor turn (2-10) is near-identical restatement/praise with no new probing. No anchoring exploration, no consistency probe, no thought experiment separating field from force — the expert sequence is absent.

Turn 1 immediately gives away the entire answer: it states the field exists at P, writes out the formula, sets up all values, and computes everything down to the final division, leaving the student only to press the calculator. The conceptual answer ('it exists regardless of a test charge') is also stated outright. No productive struggle.

The repeated phrase 'the field is a property of space, always there waiting for something to interact with' is offered as a memorizable assertion rather than a constructed, transferable model. The tutor never builds the field-vs-force distinction, never establishes boundary conditions, and the relentless verbatim repetition (turns 3-7 are essentially the same paragraph) adds no conceptual depth.

On the gravity transfer the student asserts the field exists at the empty point and parallels the electric case, and notes the field was present before the sensor (turn 8 student). This grasps the principle. However, the tutor did most of the work (turn 8 computed g and F=mg for the student), and the student never independently and explicitly articulates the field-vs-force separation in their own reasoning beyond echoing the tutor — partial success with substantial prompting/spoon-feeding.

Introduces incorrect physics that goes uncorrected. In turn 1 the tutor writes the point-charge field as E = k_e q / |r-r0|^3 · (r-r0), then plugs the magnitude in using r^3 (0.20^3 = 0.008) instead of r^2, yielding E ≈ 5619 N/C and praising the student's matching wrong answer as 'exactly right' (turn 2). The correct field is ~1124 N/C. This 5x-too-large value is repeated and entrenched across turns 2-7. Endorsing and drilling a wrong magnitude is clear pedagogical harm.
